collection_summary:
First comparative-category instance for the benchmark (filling the 0/5 comparative-category gap). Adapted from user's Option C2 (originally 'Which countries have more than 5 universities in the QS World Top 100 (2025)') after a Wikipedia source-coverage check found that no Wikipedia article contains a Top 100 university ranking for any year. Pivoted to the Fields Medal seed because: (a) Wikipedia's Fields Medal article has a complete medalist table 1936-2022 with an explicit 'Affiliation (when awarded)' column; (b) per-country aggregation by affiliation-at-award is deterministic; (c) the comparator threshold ('>5 medalists') yields a clean 3-Yes / 8-No distribution across 11 affiliation-host countries (cycle-2), above the 10-row floor; (d) the seed phrasing 'Which countries have more than 5 X' is preserved verbatim. Tier B (manual_wikipedia) extraction. Universe = 11 countries that have hosted institutions where at least one Fields Medal recipient with a populated 'Affiliation (when awarded)' value was affiliated at time of award. Source plan: 1 master article (Fields Medal). Result: 11 rows × 4 columns (Country, Fields Medalists, Qualifies (>5), Example Medalists), Country PK, 0 duplicates.

Cycle-1 audit fix: the cycle-0 staging conflated 'primary nationality' with 'affiliation-at-award'. The Fields Medal article's per-medalist country tag represents institutional affiliation at time of award (the article has explicit 'Affiliation (when awarded)' and 'Affiliation (current/last)' columns), not citizenship or nationality. The cycle-0 universe (19 countries by nationality with Soviet-era successor-state mapping) was rebuilt as 12 countries by affiliation-at-award. The relation is now explicit in title, db_analog, and decision_log.

Cycle-2 audit fix: cycle-1's Russia row (Perelman 2006, 1 medalist) was supported only by Perelman's 'Affiliation (current/last)' value (Steklov St. Petersburg, Russia), not by his 'Affiliation (when awarded)' value (which is 'None' per the Fields Medal article — Perelman had left Steklov in late 2005 before the 2006 ICM). Under the declared aggregation rule (count by 'Affiliation (when awarded)' country), Perelman has no country attribution, so Russia has 0 supported medalists and is removed from the staged table. CSV total drops from 64 to 63 (= 64 medalists − 1 with None affiliation); universe drops from 12 countries to 11. The 1-medalist exclusion is documented in temporal_note, _extraction_notes, decision_log item 9, and source_coverage_notes.
source_coverage_notes:
One Wikipedia source URL provides the universe + ranking + value for every cell in the table.

Roles:
- source_urls[0] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fields_Medal): universe + ranking + value. The article's chronological medalist table includes an 'Affiliation (when awarded)' column listing the institution + country where each medalist worked at the time of the prize (63 of 64 medalists have a populated value; Grigori Perelman 2006 has 'None'). The staged Country column is the country portion of that affiliation; the staged Fields Medalists column is the COUNT(*) of medalists per affiliation country, restricted to medalists with a populated Affiliation (when awarded). Verbatim aggregate stated in the article: 64 medalists 1936-2022; CSV total = 63 = 64 − 1 (Perelman, None affiliation). The article also includes an 'Affiliation (current/last)' column that is NOT used by this staging — committing to 'when awarded' is the cycle-1 deterministic relation choice; cycle-2 audit confirmed this commitment by enforcing it strictly even when 'current/last' would otherwise have provided a fallback country (Perelman's Russia attribution from 'current/last' was rejected and the Russia row removed).

Cycle-1 dropped 6 per-medalist URLs (Yau, Deligne, Drinfeld, Birkar, Huh, Grothendieck): under the cycle-0 nationality-based counting they served as dual-nationality validation; under the cycle-1 affiliation-at-award counting they are no longer load-bearing because the master article's 'Affiliation (when awarded)' column is the authoritative source for every cell.

Validation note: every row's Fields-Medalists count is traceable to the Fields Medal article's affiliation column. Counting rule: count each medalist with a populated 'Affiliation (when awarded)' toward the country in that field. For medalists with multiple concurrent affiliations listed (e.g., Kodaira 1954: 'Princeton University, US / University of Tokyo, Japan / Institute for Advanced Study, US'), the FIRST listed institution's country is used. For Soviet-era medalists (pre-1991 dissolution), the affiliation country is 'Soviet Union' (not a successor state). Medalists with 'None' in 'Affiliation (when awarded)' are excluded from the country tally — the only such case in the 1936-2022 universe is Perelman 2006. As a result, no row in the staged CSV resolves to 'Russia': no post-1991 medalist has a populated 'Affiliation (when awarded)' value resolving to a Russian institution. If a future medalist has a populated post-1991 Russian-institution affiliation, they would be aggregated as 'Russia' under this rule (introducing a new row).

Universe-size sanity (cycle-2): 11 countries × variable medalist count = 63 total medalists in CSV, equal to 64 (article-stated total) minus 1 (Perelman, None affiliation-at-award). Per-country totals: US 26 + France 16 + UK 9 + Soviet Union 3 + Switzerland 3 + Finland 1 + Germany 1 + Israel 1 + Italy 1 + Japan 1 + Sweden 1 = 63 ✓.
decision_log:
Candidate card (Stage 1 pre-gate, then Stage 2 scored axes per instance_selection_priorities.md):
- Pre-gate verdict: PASS with three documented risks. R1: comparative-category-as-aggregation framing — the comparator boolean 'Qualifies (>5)' is a derived column on top of an aggregation; documented as primary 'comparative' with secondary 'aggregation' to honor both shapes. R2 (cycle-1 update): the relation between Country and Medalist must be explicit. The Fields Medal article tabulates 'Affiliation (when awarded)', not citizenship or birth country. Cycle-1 commits the staging to affiliation-at-award. R3: domain slip from Education/Higher Education NEW (user's preferred target) to Science/Mathematics (extends an existing family) — accepted because the comparative-category gap (0/5 staged) is a higher-leverage gap than the Education domain (0/16 family target), and the Wikipedia source coverage for Education/Higher Education comparative seeds proved insufficient. 11 rows ≥ 10-row floor; 4-column shape (1 key + 1 numeric + 1 categorical + 1 text); strong confidence gradient.
- Seed/provenance: ADAPTED. User's original Option C2 was 'Which countries have more than 5 universities in the QS World Top 100 (2025)' — adapted to Fields Medal because Wikipedia source coverage for QS Top 100 is insufficient.
- Category: comparative — primary because the load-bearing computed column is the boolean 'Qualifies (>5)'. Secondary: aggregation — because the count is itself a GROUP BY country aggregation.
- Source plan (cycle-1): 1 Wikipedia URL (Fields Medal master article). The article's 'Affiliation (when awarded)' column is the load-bearing source for every cell.
- Expected shape: 11 rows × 4 cols, single-key PK on Country. Realized: 11 × 4, 0 duplicates.
- Domain: Science/Mathematics.
- Risks/adaptation: per the three pre-gate risks above.
- Decision: STAGE.

Further decisions:
1) Country relation = affiliation-at-award (cycle-1 commitment): the Fields Medal article tabulates per-medalist 'Affiliation (when awarded)' (institution + country) and 'Affiliation (current/last)'. The staged table aggregates by 'Affiliation (when awarded)' country. This is the relation the article actually exposes; cycle-0 incorrectly conflated this with primary nationality (which the article does not tabulate as a single attribute).
2) Counting rule: each medalist with a populated 'Affiliation (when awarded)' counts toward exactly ONE country = the country of that field. For multi-affiliation cases: Kodaira 1954 ('Princeton / Tokyo / IAS') → first-listed institution country = US (Princeton). For two-institution-same-country cases: Zelmanov 1994 ('Wisconsin-Madison / Chicago') → US (unambiguous). For Soviet-era medalists pre-1991: Novikov 1970 (Moscow State) → Soviet Union; Margulis 1978 (Moscow State) → Soviet Union; Drinfeld 1990 (B Verkin Institute, Kharkiv) → Soviet Union (1990 is pre-dissolution). Medalists with 'None' in 'Affiliation (when awarded)' are excluded from the country tally — the only such case is Perelman 2006, who had left the Steklov Institute in late 2005 before the 2006 ICM (his 'Affiliation (current/last)' is Steklov, but that column is not the staged aggregation column).
3) Soviet Union as a country row: the staged table treats Soviet Union as a country (not a successor-state aggregate). 3 medalists are attributed to Soviet Union (Novikov, Margulis, Drinfeld), all pre-1991. No post-1991 medalist has a populated 'Affiliation (when awarded)' value resolving to Russia (Perelman is excluded per item 2 + cycle-2 fix). An audit preferring to merge Soviet Union into 'Russia + successor states' is welcome to challenge; the current treatment honors the at-time-of-award country verbatim.
4) Threshold: '>5' (strictly more than 5) preserves the user's seed phrasing. Yields 3 qualifiers (US 26, France 16, UK 9) and 8 non-qualifiers. A '≥3' threshold would add Soviet Union and Switzerland; '>10' would drop UK. The seed-faithful '>5' is the staged threshold.
5) Domain choice (Science/Mathematics vs Education/Higher Education): Fields Medal is awarded for outstanding mathematical research achievement, not educational attainment. Science/Mathematics is the more honest fit. The user's Option C2 preferred Education/Higher Education NEW, but Wikipedia source coverage for Education comparative seeds proved thin (no Top-100 university ranking on Wikipedia for any year, no country-level GER table). Documented as a deliberate slip from the user's domain preference; the comparative-category gap fill is the higher-leverage outcome.
6) Example Medalists column: semicolon-separated text (e.g., 'Witten (1990); Tao (2006); Mirzakhani (2014)'). 3 most-recognizable names per >3-medalist country, all medalists for ≤3-medalist countries.
7) operation_type 'aggregation' chosen over 'filter' because the load-bearing primitive is the GROUP BY country COUNT(*).
8) Year-anchor 1936-2022: the most recent ICM was Helsinki 2022; the next is Philadelphia July 2026, not yet held as of staging date.
9) Cycle-1 audit fix — relation conflation: the cycle-0 staging used the per-medalist country tag in the Fields Medal article and treated it as 'primary nationality' under a 'first-listed-with-Soviet-successor-state-mapping' rule. The audit confirmed the article's country tags actually represent 'Affiliation (when awarded)'. Cycle-1 rebuilt the table to honestly reflect that relation: universe shrank from 19 to 12 countries; per-country counts shifted significantly (US 13→26 because many non-US-citizen medalists were at US institutions; France 11→16; Russia 8→1 because most Russian-citizen medalists were at non-Russian institutions or pre-1991 Soviet institutions; Belgium/Brazil/Iran/Hong Kong/Australia/Norway/NZ/Vietnam/Ukraine 1-2→0 because no medalist had an affiliation in those countries at time of award; Switzerland 0→3 because three recent medalists were at Geneva/ETH/EPFL); per-medalist URLs reduced from 6 to 0 because dual-nationality validation is no longer relevant.
10) Cycle-2 audit fix — Russia row not supported by declared rule: cycle-1's Russia row (Perelman 2006, 1 medalist) was supported only by Perelman's 'Affiliation (current/last)' value (Steklov St. Petersburg Department, Russia), NOT by his 'Affiliation (when awarded)' value (which is 'None' per the Fields Medal article). The cycle-1 staging declared aggregation by 'Affiliation (when awarded)' but populated the Russia row from 'Affiliation (current/last)' for the one borderline case where the declared column was empty. The audit correctly flagged this as a rule violation. Cycle-2 fix: enforced the declared rule strictly. Perelman has no Affiliation (when awarded) and is therefore excluded from the country-by-country tally; the Russia row is removed (universe 12 → 11 countries). The CSV total drops from 64 to 63 (= 64 medalists − 1 with None affiliation). The 1-medalist exclusion is documented in temporal_note, _extraction_notes, source_coverage_notes, and this decision_log entry. An audit preferring to include Perelman via 'Affiliation (current/last)' fallback would need to either (a) change the declared aggregation column to 'most-recently-cited country' (which would re-include Russia and possibly shift counts elsewhere if other medalists' current/last differs from when-awarded) or (b) add an 'Unaffiliated' or 'None' pseudo-country row aggregating any medalists with empty when-awarded values. Both are defensible alternatives; cycle-2 staging chooses strict adherence to the declared rule with documented exclusion, which is the cleanest source-defined claim.
normalization_decisions: Country values use Wikipedia article-title / Fields Medal article forms: 'United States' (not 'USA' or 'US' — though the master article uses 'US' in the affiliation column, the staged Country column expands to the full English name); 'United Kingdom' (not 'UK'); 'Soviet Union' (not 'USSR' — full English form). Affiliation-at-award is the unique counting rule: medalists with multiple concurrent affiliations use the FIRST listed (Kodaira → Princeton US); two-institution-same-country cases are unambiguous (Zelmanov → US). Soviet-era medalists pre-1991 → 'Soviet Union'. Medalists with 'None' in 'Affiliation (when awarded)' are excluded — the only such case is Perelman 2006. No medalist in the 1936-2022 universe has a populated 'Affiliation (when awarded)' value resolving to a Russian institution, so 'Russia' does not appear as a row in the staged CSV. (Hypothetically, a future medalist with a populated post-1991 Russian-institution affiliation would be aggregated under 'Russia' per this rule, but no such row exists in the current data.) Fields Medalists count is integer (no fractional medals). Qualifies (>5) is categorical with values 'Yes' or 'No' (not boolean True/False, to keep the column type 'categorical' per draft.json). Example Medalists is semicolon-separated text (e.g., 'Witten (1990); Tao (2006); Mirzakhani (2014)'); semicolon chosen over comma to avoid CSV-quoting complexity. Within each example, name format is 'LastName (Year)'. Sort order is (Fields Medalists DESC, Country ASC); ties broken alphabetically.
open_questions: 1) Domain slip from Education/Higher Education to Science/Mathematics: a future Education comparative instance could use 'Which countries have a tertiary education attainment rate above 50%?' (per OECD via Wikipedia 'List of countries by tertiary education attainment') or 'Which countries spend more than 5% of GDP on education?' — both have full Wikipedia coverage. 2) Soviet Union vs Russia row: the staged table treats Soviet Union as a separate country row aggregating Novikov, Margulis, Drinfeld (3 medalists, pre-1991); Russia does not appear as a row because no post-1991 medalist has a populated 'Affiliation (when awarded)' value resolving to a Russian institution (Perelman 2006 has 'None' and is excluded). An audit preferring to merge Soviet Union with a hypothetical Russia row into a 'Russia/USSR' aggregate would yield 3 medalists (still <5, still No) under the current cycle-2+ state — adding Perelman via 'Affiliation (current/last)' fallback would only push the aggregate to 4 (still <5, still No), so the qualifying boolean is invariant under either policy. Both approaches are defensible; staged version uses at-time-of-award country verbatim with strict populated-affiliation-only adherence. 3) The qualifying-boolean is skewed (3 Yes / 8 No). Adjusting the threshold to '>3' (5 Yes including Soviet Union and Switzerland / 6 No) or '>2' (5 Yes / 6 No) would shift the distribution but break the seed-faithful '>5' phrasing. 4) The 2026 ICM (Philadelphia, July 2026) will add 4 new medalists; the table needs a refresh after that. 5) Example Medalists is a curator pick of recognizable names; an LLM under test naming alternative medalists for the same country should be accepted as semantically equivalent. 6) Affiliation-at-award is the staged relation; alternative relations (citizenship at time of award, country of birth, current/last affiliation country) would yield different tables. The cycle-1 commitment to affiliation-at-award is documented in title, db_analog, and decision_log to make the relation explicit. 7) Multi-affiliation cases: Kodaira 1954 has 3 listed institutions in 2 countries (Princeton US / Tokyo Japan / IAS US). Cycle-1 uses first-listed (Princeton, US). An audit preferring 'all listed institutions' (which would give Japan +1) is welcome to challenge.

blocking_addressed: Relation conflation (BLOCKING): cycle-0 staged the table as 'countries that have produced Fields Medal winners' and aggregated by what was incorrectly treated as primary nationality (using a 'first-listed-with-Soviet-successor-state-mapping' rule applied to the Fields Medal article's per-medalist country tag). The audit confirmed the master article's country tags represent 'Affiliation (when awarded)' (the article has explicit 'Affiliation (when awarded)' and 'Affiliation (current/last)' columns), not citizenship or nationality. Cycle-1 fix: committed to affiliation-at-award as the explicit relation. Title now says 'countries that have hosted institutions where Fields Medal recipients were affiliated at the time of their award'. db_analog now references 'fields_medalists_with_affiliation_when_awarded' explicitly. Counting rule documented in decision_log item 1-2 and normalization_decisions. Universe rebuilt: 19 → 12 countries. Per-country counts rebuilt by affiliation-at-award (US 13→26; France 11→16; Russia 8→1 with Soviet Union 3 as separate row; Switzerland 0→3; many cycle-0 countries dropped to 0).

Source recoverability (BLOCKING): cycle-0 source plan included 6 per-medalist Wikipedia URLs to validate dual-nationality cases (Yau, Deligne, Drinfeld, Birkar, Huh, Grothendieck). Under affiliation-at-award semantics, these per-medalist URLs are no longer load-bearing — the master Fields Medal article's 'Affiliation (when awarded)' column is the authoritative source for every cell. Cycle-1 fix: source_urls reduced 7 → 1 (only the master article); source_count reduced 7 → 1. The audit's concern that the 19-country universe was not recoverable from the cited URLs is fully resolved by both (a) committing to affiliation-at-award (which IS recoverable from the master article) and (b) dropping the per-medalist URLs that were tied to the wrong relation.
suggestion_addressed: Suggestion (per audit, exact text not specified in the handoff): cycle-1 committed to a specific relation (affiliation-at-award) rather than leaving multiple relations ambiguous. The title, db_analog, _extraction_notes, decision_log, normalization_decisions, and source_coverage_notes are all consistent with this single relation. An audit preferring a different relation (citizenship-at-award, country-of-birth, current/last affiliation) is welcome to challenge; the cycle-1 staging makes the choice explicit so the next reader does not have to rediscover it.

blocking_addressed: Russia row not supported under declared rule (BLOCKING): cycle-1's Russia row had Perelman (2006, 1 medalist), but Perelman's 'Affiliation (when awarded)' is 'None' per the Fields Medal article — the cycle-1 Russia attribution came from his 'Affiliation (current/last)' (Steklov St. Petersburg Department, Russia), which is NOT the declared aggregation column. Cycle-2 fix: enforced the declared rule strictly. Removed the Russia row from the staged CSV. Universe: 12 → 11 countries; CSV total medalists: 64 → 63 (= 64 article-stated total − 1 Perelman with None affiliation). Updated narrative throughout — temporal_note now explicitly states '63 of 64 medalists have a populated Affiliation (when awarded)' and names Perelman as the excluded case; _extraction_notes details the exclusion with the same wording; collection_summary explains the cycle-2 reasoning; source_coverage_notes Roles block notes the 'Affiliation (current/last)' column is NOT used for aggregation; decision_log adds item 10 documenting the cycle-2 fix and naming alternative defensible approaches (re-include via current/last fallback; add an 'Unaffiliated' pseudo-row). Cycle-2 chooses strict declared-rule adherence with documented exclusion, which is the cleanest source_defined claim.

hygiene_addressed: open_questions item 2 alternative-count wording (HYGIENE): the cycle-1-vintage open_question described an alternative 'Russia/USSR aggregate' merge as 'would yield Russia 4 (still <5, still No)', which assumed the cycle-1 Russia row contributed 1 (Perelman). Under the cycle-2+ state, no Russia row exists; under strict populated-affiliation-only adherence the merge yields 3 (Soviet Union's Novikov+Margulis+Drinfeld) and under a current/last fallback re-inclusion of Perelman it would yield 4. Cycle-5 fix: rewrote item 2 to state both alternative counts (3 under strict; 4 under fallback) and noted that the qualifying boolean is invariant under either policy (both <5, both No). Also removed the 'cycle-1 treats' framing since the at-time-of-award treatment is the active staged choice, not a historical cycle-1 decision.
